about.title: Rancho Santa Margarita Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Rancho Santa Margarita households rely on everyday products — from household appliances to vehicle parts used along Santa Margarita Parkway and Antonio Parkway — and most work as intended. But when a manufacturing flaw, design mistake, or missing warning label causes harm, the injured person shouldn't have to untangle corporate supply chains alone. California law generally allows product liability claims to proceed under a strict liability standard, meaning you don't have to prove the manufacturer was careless, only that the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This applies whether the harm came from a kitchen appliance, a piece of exercise equipment, a car part, or a tool used at home or on the job. LawProactive doesn't practice law; we simply connect Rancho Santa Margarita residents with an independent attorney who can evaluate what happened, help preserve the product as evidence, and explain the options that may be available at no upfront cost to you.

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Case
items.desc: California generally lets injured people pursue product liability claims without proving negligence — only that the product was defective and caused harm. An attorney can help identify whether the defect was in design, manufacturing, or warnings.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable under California law. This broadens the possible sources of recovery for someone injured by a defective product.

items.title: Evidence Preservation Matters Early
items.desc: Because the product itself is often central evidence, an attorney can advise on how to safely store it rather than repair, discard, or lose it before it can be examined.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was negligent?
items.answer: Generally, no. California product liability law often applies a strict liability standard, meaning the focus is on whether the product was defective and caused your injury, not on proving carelessness. An independent attorney can review the specifics of your situation to explain how this applies.

items.question: What should I do with the product that hurt me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the condition it was in right after the incident, including packaging, receipts, or manuals if you have them. Avoid repairing or discarding it, since the product itself is often key evidence. An attorney can guide you on safe storage and next steps.
